transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I’m just tired all the time. It's... by midmorning at work, after just reviewing files or maybe walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it feels like my body and my brain are already running on empty. I just don't have the energy I should.
Do you also feel sad or down when you're tired like that?

Yeah, I do. It's... well, most days I just feel like there’s a gray film over everything. Even when things are fine, like if my husband is being really kind to me, or we’re cooking together with the family... I just kind of go through the motions. I don't really feel the enjoyment I used to.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been quite a while now. Um, I'd say about three years... maybe three years and three months. It really started right around the time I was moved into a higher-responsibility role at work. That was when they had me start mentoring the junior adjusters and overseeing the new workflow systems.
Do you find yourself losing interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes, I definitely have. Um... outside of work, I've pretty much pulled back from everything. I used to do a lot of painting, hiking, and some volunteering, but... I just don't have the drive for it anymore. I'm honestly just trying to get through the week. 

And it's affecting my job, too. I've noticed I'm starting to miss details in my audits, and... well, it's taking me a lot longer to sign off on files than it used to. It just takes everything I have just to keep up.
Do you still enjoy the things you do, even if you don't have the energy to do them?

No, not really. Even when I do manage to push myself to do something, like... going for a walk or trying to paint for a few minutes, it just feels flat. I don't get that spark or satisfaction out of it anymore. It just feels like another chore I have to get through.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

No, I haven't really noticed any big changes. My weight has stayed pretty much the same. I guess I eat about the same amount as I usually do, even if I don't really care about what I'm eating most of the time.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

No, not really. My sleep has been pretty normal. I usually go to bed at my regular time and get, you know, seven or eight hours. So I haven't really noticed any problems with falling asleep or staying asleep.
Do you have difficulty concentrating on things, like when you're reviewing files at work?
No, I haven't really noticed any trouble with that. When I'm at work looking over claims, I can still focus on the files just fine. My concentration seems to be okay.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Honestly, no... not really. I can't think of anything that I actually get pleasure out of these days. I just kind of go to work, come home, and that's about it. Nothing really stands out as being enjoyable anymore.
Have you ever felt so down that you thought you'd be better off dead?
No, I haven't. I mean, I feel down most of the time, obviously, but... no, I've never actually thought I'd be better off dead. It doesn't get to that extreme. I don't have thoughts like that.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently depressed?

Yes, definitely. It's been going on for much longer than two weeks, honestly. Most days I just feel like there’s... a gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being really kind, or we’re cooking with the family, I just kind of go through the motions. I don't really feel the enjoyment I used to feel. It's just a constant, down feeling that's almost always there.
Do you feel like your depressive feelings are consistently worse than they are better?

I'm not exactly sure how to measure that. I haven't really noticed them getting worse or better, to be honest. Like I said, it's just... a constant low. I don't really have days where I feel good, so it's hard to say if it's worse than it is better. It's just always kind of that same flat feeling.
Have you noticed any difference in the intensity of your depressive feelings over time?

No, not really. Um... it's pretty much like I was just saying. It doesn't really go up or down in intensity. It's just... steady. I don't really have times where it feels a lot heavier, and I don't have times where it suddenly lifts. It's just been this same flat feeling for a long time now.
Do you find that your low mood or energy levels change at certain times of the year?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. It doesn't seem to matter if it's summer or winter, or holidays or anything. The mood just stays the same year-round. Like I said, it's just a steady, flat feeling no matter what the calendar says.
Would you say your depressive feelings are interfering with your daily life a lot or just a little?

I'd say a moderate amount. It's definitely affecting things. At work, I've started missing details in my audits, and it's taking me a lot longer to sign off on files than it used to. And outside of work... I've just pulled back from a lot of things. I used to paint, go hiking, volunteer, but I've stopped doing all of that. Honestly, I'm just trying to get through the week.

Would you describe your low mood as mild, where you're still able to function and find some interest in activities, or moderate, where it's more pronounced and interferes with your daily life more significantly?

I'd definitely say moderate. Like I was just saying, it's really interfering with my work and my life. I'm not really finding interest in anything anymore, and I've stopped doing all the things I used to enjoy. So, yeah, it's definitely more than just a mild feeling.
